title: Quarter the total batch size (2^19 -> 2^17)
description: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**17 and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 -> 64 (grad_accum stays 1); all LRs and schedules untouched.
reflection: val_bpb 0.997280 vs 0.997333 baseline - a 5e-5 move, i.e. a tie, not a win. The run did 3153 optimizer steps on 413.3M tokens at 33.2% MFU. That is the important number: the baseline at 2^19 gets ~790 steps on the same ~413M tokens, so quadrupling the number of updates changed val_bpb by nothing. The premise five of six of us proposed this round - that a 5-minute run is step-limited - is simply false. Token throughput, not update count, sets the loss here; the batch axis is flat from 2^19 down to at least 2^17 and should be closed. Two things I noticed that look more promising than anything on the batch axis: MFU is only 33%, so most of the card is being left on the floor, and peak VRAM is 22.7GB of 80GB, so there is no memory pressure at all. Whatever buys tokens/sec (or spends the idle capacity on a bigger/better-shaped model) is where the remaining headroom is.
